papers.title_zh: 托珠单抗用于重症汉坦病毒肺综合征的研究:MEURI病例系列及情境比较。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒肺综合征是一种罕见的动物源性疾病,死亡率高,伴有严重的全身性炎症。
analysis_zh.methods: 在阿根廷巴里洛切地区医院 Dr Ramón Carrillo 进行描述性病例系列研究;实验室确诊的重症 汉坦病毒肺综合征、需入ICU的患者符合MEURI框架下托珠单抗使用条件;在入ICU后24小时内给予单剂量静脉注射8 mg/kg(最高800 mg)。
analysis_zh.results: 2024年6月1日至2026年5月5日期间,共评估13例患者;其中10例符合入选标准,5例接受托珠单抗治疗,5例未接受。接受治疗的5例中有4例存活至ICU出院,而未治疗的5例全部死亡。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究结果提示IL‐6抑制可能提升重症 汉坦病毒肺综合征 患者的存活率,值得在MEURI或扩大使用框架下进一步评估。
analysis_zh.limitations: 目前尚无特异性抗病毒或免疫调节疗法被证实可常规使用,这限制了对上述观察结果的解释背景。

papers.title: Hantavirus risk and preparedness in Europe in an era of climate change and global mobility.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonoses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. In Europe, Puumala virus (PUUV) and Dobrava virus (DOBV) account for most recognized disease; Seoul virus (SEOV) is relevant to ports and urban settings. The 2026 MV Hondius cruise-ship cluster of Andes hantavirus (ANDV) infections, involving passengers from 23 countries, has highlighted urgent gaps in European preparedness for both endemic and imported hantavirus disease. OBJECTIVES: To review hantavirus epidemiology, ecology, clinical recognition, diagnostics, and preparedness in Europe, with emphasis on endemic PUUV, DOBV, and SEOV, and to clarify the separate relevance of imported ANDV infection for travel medicine and maritime response. SOURCES: We conducted a structured narrative review of literature published from January 2000 to May 2026, prioritizing surveillance reports, systematic and narrative reviews, rodent ecology studies, diagnostic evaluations, external quality assessment studies, and outbreak investigations. WHO, European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, and International Health Regulations guidance documents were also reviewed. CONTENT: European hantavirus epidemiology is heterogeneous and shaped by reservoir ecology, biome-specific rodent dynamics, clinical awareness, diagnostic capacity, and surveillance practice. Climate effects are indirect and regionally variable, mediated by mast years, predator-prey dynamics, winter conditions, land use, reservoir density, and human exposure. Diagnostic preparedness is uneven, particularly for molecular detection. Imported ANDV infection is rare in Europe but relevant to travel medicine and high-consequence preparedness because it can cause severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and, unlike endemic European hantaviruses, has documented person-to-person transmission. IMPLICATIONS: European preparedness should prioritize PUUV, DOBV, and SEOV through rodent biomonitoring, harmonized surveillance, improved molecular diagnostics, and locally calibrated early warning.
papers.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 欧洲在气候变化和全球流动时代的风险与防备。

papers.title: Hantavirus infection in emergency radiology: Imaging manifestations, pathophysiology, and infection control considerations.
papers.abstract: In April 2026, several cases of severe respiratory illnesses were reported aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius during its voyage from Argentina. Subsequent laboratory testing identified Andes virus (ANDV), a hantavirus subtype, with rare but documented human-to-human transmission. Although hantavirus infections are uncommon, both hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Their rapid progression and potential need for intensive respiratory support continue to pose important challenges for emergency departments, intensive care units, and radiology services. Because pulmonary imaging findings often evolve quickly, radiologists play a critical role in early recognition and triage. This review provides an overview of the pathophysiology, imaging manifestations, and operational considerations relevant to hantavirus infection in emergency radiology practice.

papers.title: EPIZOOTIC AND EPIDEMIC SITUATION OF HANTAVIRUS INFECTION IN THE WORLD
papers.abstract: This review examines the current epidemiological and epizootic situation in natural foci of hantavirus diseases across various regions of the world. Today, hantavirus diseases represent a significant threat to the sanitary and epidemiological well-being of populations worldwide, capable of seriously complicating the epidemiological situation. Approximately 200,000 cases are registered worldwide annually, although the intensity and dynamics of morbidity vary considerably across regions. In China — the country with the highest annual number of cases in the world — the overall incidence trend is declining. Ukraine is a natural endemic focus for the spread of hantaviruses that cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). Given climate change, which stimulates rodent migration and reproduction, epidemiological risks for the rural population and military personnel are increasing. Data on the spread of hantavirus infection in the regions of Southeast Asia and the African continent require further study; however, it is quite evident that hantavirus infection is an underestimated public health problem in these regions, and its true scale — given the wide distribution of reservoir hosts — may be considerably greater than currently known. Keywords: hantavirus diseases, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, epidemiological situation, natural reservoirs, pathogens.

analysis_zh.background: 本综述旨在评估全球自然疫源地中 汉坦病毒 感染的流行病学和动物疫情状态。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 它强调 汉坦病毒 疾病是重大公共卫生威胁,指出气候驱动的啮齿动物动态增加风险,并指出东南亚和非洲等研究不足的地区。
analysis_zh.current_state: 全球每年约报告 200,000 例,地区间存在差异;中国发病率呈下降趋势,而乌克兰仍是 HFRS 的流行重点地区。
analysis_zh.gaps: 汉坦病毒 在东南亚和非洲的传播数据稀缺,鉴于宿主广泛存在,实际负担可能被低估。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要在东南亚和非洲开展有针对性的监测和流行病学研究,以阐明患病率、宿主生态以及气候相关的风险因素。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：本综述旨在评估全球自然疫源地中 汉坦病毒 感染的流行病学和动物疫情状态。 主要方向：它强调 汉坦病毒 疾病是重大公共卫生威胁,指出气候驱动的啮齿动物动态增加风险,并指出东南亚和非洲等研究不足的地区。 研究现状：全球每年约报告 200,000 例,地区间存在差异;中国发病率呈下降趋势,而乌克兰仍是 HFRS 的流行重点地区。 不足：汉坦病毒 在东南亚和非洲的传播数据稀缺,鉴于宿主广泛存在,实际负担可能被低估。 后续研究：需要在东南亚和非洲开展有针对性的监测和流行病学研究,以阐明患病率、宿主生态以及气候相关的风险因素。

papers.title: Multi-Country Human-to-Human Andes Virus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship: A Disaster Report on Prehospital, Health Care Facility, and Public Health System Challenges - Essential Knowledge for Frontline Clinicians.
papers.abstract: Abstract The Andes Virus (ANDV) outbreak reported on May 2, 2026, aboard a luxury vessel departing from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina, was caused by an Orthohantavirus unique in its person-to-person transmissibility in contrast to zoonotic transmission characteristic of better-known hantaviruses. Containment required coordinated international management because passengers and crew embarked and disembarked at several international ports-of-call prior to outbreak recognition, resulting in cross-border transmission potential. Among those who disembarked, several traveled on flights to various destinations. Cases subsequently manifested in multiple countries, including Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada, and The Netherlands. Upon notification, international health authorities implemented containment measures, such as contact tracing, quarantine, and isolation. Uniquely, ANDV poses distinctive risks due to its immediately prodromal presymptomatic transmission potential, initial non-specific flu-like symptoms, prolonged incubation period, conceivable long-term neurologic and endocrinologic sequalae, high case fatality rates (CFRs), and possibility of international dissemination. This report describes the successful management of a multi-national outbreak associated with cruise-ship travel, a setting with unique challenges. It also examines implications and challenges for prehospital, health care facility, and public health systems for future ANDV outbreaks. The event was characterized by delayed recognition, international spread, and complex coordination across multiple jurisdictions and sectors, including medical and public health authorities, policy- and decision-makers, crisis and emergency risk-communication experts, media, logistics, transportation, and security. Rapid implementation of public health measures coupled with clinician implementation of the Identify-Isolate-Inform (3I) model, a clinical framework to detect and prevent the spread of infectious disease, at the prehospital and health care facility levels are critical actions that can contain future ANDV outbreaks.

Event Description Event Type: Multi-Country Infectious Disease Outbreak Event Date: Index Case Boarded Ship on April 1, 2026; Outbreak Reported to the World Health Organization (WHO) on May 2, 2026; Concluded on July 2, 20261 Location: Luxury Cruise Ship MV Hondius Departing from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina Response Type: Multi-National Medical and Public Health Introduction On May 2, 2026, the United Kingdom (UK) alerted the World Health Organization (WHO; Geneva, Switzerland) of an unprecedented multi-country outbreak of an Orthohantavirus on board the luxury cruise ship MV Hondius, a vessel that can accommodate approximately 250 people, consisting of passengers and crewmembers. The ship set sail on April 1, 2026 from Ushuaia, Patagonia, an area endemic for Orthohantavirus andesense, or Andes Virus (ANDV). Orthohantavirus are enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded ribonucleic acid (RNA) viruses maintained primarily in rodent reservoirs; related hantaviruses have also been identified in bats and other small mammals. A significant number of individuals on the ship disembarked and traveled to various international destinations prior to awareness that they had been exposed to an infectious disease on board (Table 1). By the conclusion of the outbreak, there were a total of 13 cases (12 confirmed and one probable for ANDV). Marty MD1, Christian K. Beÿ MPH2 and Kristi L. Koenig MD3,4 1Florida International University, Miami, Florida, USA; 2School of Medicine, University of California, San Diego, La Jolla, California, USA; 3County of San Diego, Emergency Medical Services Office, Public Safety Group – San Diego County Fire, San Diego, California, USA and 4Department of Emergency Medicine and Public Health, University of California Irvine, Orange, California, USA Abstract The Andes Virus (ANDV) outbreak reported on May 2, 2026, aboard a luxury vessel departing from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina, was caused by an Orthohantavirus unique in its person-to- person transmissibility in contrast to zoonotic transmission characteristic of better-known hantaviruses. Containment required coordinated international management because pas- sengers and crew embarked and disembarked at several international ports-of-call prior to outbreak recognition, resulting in cross-border transmission potential. Among those who disembarked, several traveled on flights to various destinations. Cases subsequently manifested in multiple countries, including Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada, and The Netherlands. Upon notification, international health authorities implemented containment measures, such as contact tracing, quarantine, and isolation. Uniquely, ANDV poses distinctive risks due to its immediately prodromal presymptomatic transmission potential, initial non-specific flu-like symptoms, prolonged incubation period, conceivable long-term neurologic and endocrinologic sequalae, high case fatality rates (CFRs), and pos- sibility of international dissemination. This report describes the successful management of a multi-national outbreak associated with cruise-ship travel, a setting with unique challenges. It also examines implications and challenges for prehospital, health care facility, and public health systems for future ANDV outbreaks. The event was characterized by delayed recognition, international spread, and complex coordination across multiple jurisdictions and sectors, including medical and public health authorities, policy- and decision-makers, crisis and emergency risk-communication experts, media, logistics, transportation, and security. Rapid implementation of public health measures coupled with clinician implementation of the Identify-Isolate-Inform (3I) model, a clinical framework to detect and prevent the spread of infectious disease, at the prehospital and health care facility levels are critical actions that can contain future ANDV outbreaks. analysis.summary_en: Background: The Andes Virus (ANDV) outbreak on a luxury cruise ship departed from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina, and was notable for its person‑to‑person transmissibility, a feature unique among hantaviruses, presenting distinctive risks including presymptomatic transmission, non‑specific flu‑like symptoms, prolonged incubation, potential long‑term sequelae, high case fatality rates, and international dissemination. Methods: Containment required coordinated international management because passengers and crew embarked and disembarked at multiple international ports, creating cross‑border transmission potential. Several disembarked individuals traveled on flights to various destinations. Cases subsequently manifested in multiple countries, and international health authorities implemented containment measures such as contact tracing, quarantine, and isolation. Results: Cross‑border spread was documented, with cases appearing in Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada, and the Netherlands. The outbreak prompted rapid implementation of public health measures and the Identify‑Isolate‑Inform (3I) clinical framework. Contribution: The report demonstrates successful management of a multi‑national ANDV outbreak linked to cruise‑ship travel and highlights the importance of the 3I model and coordinated prehospital, health‑care facility, and public‑health responses for future outbreaks. Limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis_zh.background: 安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 在一艘豪华邮轮上的暴发,该邮轮从阿根廷巴塔哥尼亚的乌斯怀亚出发,因其人际传播能力而显著,这在 汉坦病毒 中是唯一的特征 (A1)。ANDV 具有独特风险,包括潜伏期前传播、非特异性流感样症状、潜伏期延长、可能的长期后遗症、高致死率以及国际传播 (A6)。

papers.title: Of mice and men: Updates on hantavirus disease and diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are a diverse and widespread group of zoonotic viruses under the Orthohantavirus genus that can cause severe acute cardiopulmonary or renal disease. Hantavirus species are grouped generally as either New World or Old World based on geographic distribution, which is influenced by their respective host reservoir including rodents. Although there is no specific treatment for hantaviruses, recognizing clinical presentation and interpreting laboratory results for case identification can improve patient management. Here we review the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and diagnostic testing options for hantavirus infection.

papers.title: Andes Virus - A Clinical Review.
papers.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV) is the sole orthohantavirus with documented human-to-human transmission. We summarize the epidemiology and clinical features of ANDV infection and review best practices in clinical management, as based on published expert consensus guidelines, field experience, and clinical trials. We also evaluate currently available and investigational treatments (including the use of antiviral agents), assess emerging monoclonal antibody therapies, and outline prospects for vaccine development. Finally, we discuss important infection prevention and control measures.
papers.journal: The New England journal of medicine

papers.title: Hantavirus Infection Beyond the Lung: A Multi-Organ Radiological Perspective on Diagnosis, Imaging Modalities, and Precautionary Measures for Radiology Departments.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus infection is an emerging zoonotic disease with worldwide relevance, associated with significant morbidity and mortality through hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. After recent reports, including a cluster of severe cases reported to the World Health Organization in 2026, increasing attention has been directed toward its clinical, pathological, and radiological spectrum. Radiology departments, as one of the most important health care providers involved in imaging for disease confirmation, detection of complications, and assessment of involvement of different body organs, should be familiar with the manifestations of suspected patients, the most appropriate imaging requests, and the precautionary measures required within the department to prevent disease transmission to both health care personnel and other patients undergoing imaging procedures. Therefore, in this review, we aimed to present recent clinical and radiological findings, as well as precautionary interventions that should be implemented in radiology departments.
papers.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR

papers.title: Beyond the Kidney and Lung: Cutaneous and Mucosal Clues to Human Hantavirus Disease.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne viruses that cause two overlapping vascular syndromes in humans: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, including nephropathia epidemica, and hantavirus pulmonary/cardiopulmonary syndrome. Although dermatologists are rarely central to hantavirus care, early visible abnormalities may occur on the skin, mucosa, and ocular surface. This narrative review synthesizes the dermatologic and mucocutaneous manifestations of human hantavirus disease, with emphasis on signs that should prompt diagnostic suspicion in dermatology, emergency, travel-medicine, and infectious-disease settings. The dermatologic signal is strongest in hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, where facial or upper-torso flushing, conjunctival and pharyngeal injection, petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, and mucosal bleeding may appear during the febrile or hemorrhagic phases. These findings are not pathognomonic, but their diagnostic value increases when they occur with rodent or outbreak exposure, thrombocytopenia or coagulopathy, and renal abnormalities such as proteinuria, hematuria, or acute kidney injury. In hantavirus pulmonary/cardiopulmonary syndrome, particularly infections caused by New World hantaviruses, visible cutaneous involvement is less prominent and may be absent despite severe pulmonary endothelial disease. We propose a practical dermatology-oriented trigger for suspicion based on exposure history, abrupt febrile illness, nephro-pulmonary involvement, thrombocytopenia, and vascular mucocutaneous findings. Hantavirus should be considered when otherwise unexplained vascular skin or mucosal signs occur in a febrile patient with thrombocytopenia, renal involvement, hypoxemia, or compatible exposure. The skin rarely diagnoses hantavirus alone, but it may shorten time to testing, supportive care, and public-health notification.

analysis.background: Hantaviruses cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary/cardiopulmonary syndrome (HPS), prompting a review of non‑renal, non‑pulmonary signs.
analysis.main_directions: The review highlights dermatologic, mucosal, and ocular manifestations that may appear early in hantavirus infection, especially in HFRS, and discusses their relevance for clinicians in dermatology, emergency, travel‑medicine, and infectious‑disease settings.
analysis.current_state: Facial flushing, conjunctival/pharyngeal injection, petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, and mucosal bleeding are the most frequent skin findings in HFRS, whereas cutaneous signs are often absent in New World HPS.
analysis.gaps: These cutaneous signs are not pathognomonic and their diagnostic utility is limited without supporting exposure history, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, or renal abnormalities.
analysis.future_research: The authors propose a dermatology‑oriented trigger algorithm and call for studies validating its sensitivity and specificity to accelerate testing, supportive care, and public‑health reporting.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses cause HFRS and HPS, leading to a review of skin and mucosal clues. Main directions: The review surveys early dermatologic, mucosal, and ocular signs, especially in HFRS, for clinicians across specialties. Current state: Typical findings include facial flushing, conjunctival/pharyngeal injection, petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, and mucosal bleeding in HFRS, while New World HPS often lacks skin involvement. Gaps: These signs are not pathognomonic and require corroborating exposure, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, or renal data. Future research: A dermatology‑focused trigger algorithm should be validated to improve early diagnosis, care, and public‑health response.

papers.title_zh: 超越肾脏和肺部:人类汉坦病毒疾病的皮肤和黏膜线索。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒导致 肾综合征出血热(HFRS)和 汉坦病毒 肺/心肺综合征(HPS),促使对非肾、非肺体征进行回顾。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 该回顾强调皮肤、黏膜和眼部表现,可能在 汉坦病毒 感染早期出现,尤其在 HFRS 中,并讨论其对皮肤科、急诊、旅行医学和传染病临床医生的意义。
analysis_zh.current_state: 面部潮红、结膜/咽部充血、点状出血、紫癜、瘀斑和黏膜出血是 HFRS 最常见的皮肤表现,而新世界 HPS 常缺乏皮肤体征。
analysis_zh.gaps: 这些皮肤体征并非特征性,若缺乏暴露史、血小板减少、凝血功能障碍或肾异常,其诊断价值有限。
analysis_zh.future_research: 作者提出基于皮肤科的触发算法,并呼吁开展验证其灵敏度和特异性的研究,以加快检测、支持性治疗和公共卫生报告。

papers.title: Characteristics and Superspreading Potential of Andes Virus Person-to-Person Transmission.
papers.abstract: By using historical contact tracing data, we estimated that 23.4% of case-patients caused 80% of Andes virus (ANDV) person-to-person transmission. We demonstrated a low but nonnegligible probability of observing a large-scale ANDV infection outbreak in a rodent-free setting consisting of close contacts, despite the historically self-limited person-to-person transmission of ANDV.

papers.title: Could bradykinin pathway inhibition change the course of severe hantavirus disease?
papers.abstract: A recent multi-country hantavirus outbreak associated with a cruise ship underscores the urgent need to understand the mechanisms driving severe vascular leakage and multi-organ failure. While disease severity is largely attributed to a dysregulated host immune response and intense cytokine surge, the precise molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Laboratory evidence indicates that hantavirus infection activates the factor XII-dependent kallikrein-kinin system, leading to elevated bradykinin production and subsequent endothelial barrier dysfunction. This translational mechanism is tentatively supported by two clinical case reports where severe hantavirus infections were successfully treated with the bradykinin receptor antagonist icatibant. We hypothesize that exaggerated bradykinin signalling drives the vascular leak phenotype, making the kallikrein-kinin pathway a compelling therapeutic target. Ultimately, effectively combating hantavirus-induced vascular permeability may require a multi-faceted approach combining targeted bradykinin inhibition with broader immunomodulatory strategies.

Laboratory evidence indicates that hantavirus infection activates the factor XII-dependent kallikrein-kinin system, leading to elevated bradykinin production and subsequent endothelial barrier dysfunction. This translational mechanism is tentatively supported by two clinical case reports where severe hantavirus infections were successfully treated with the bradykinin receptor antagonist icatibant. We hypothesize that exaggerated bradykinin signalling drives the vascular leak phenotype, making the kallikrein-kinin pathway a compelling therapeutic target. Ultimately, effectively combating hantavirus-induced vascular permeability may require a multi-faceted approach combining targeted bradykinin inhibition with broader immunomodulatory strategies.

analysis.methods: not reported in the supplied evidence
analysis.results: Laboratory evidence shows hantavirus activates the factor XII‑dependent kallikrein‑kinin system, raising bradykinin levels and causing endothelial barrier dysfunction; two clinical case reports describe successful treatment of severe hantavirus infection with the bradykinin receptor antagonist icatibant.
analysis.contribution: The letter proposes exaggerated bradykinin signalling as a driver of vascular leak and suggests the kallikrein‑kinin pathway as a therapeutic target, providing a translational hypothesis for future research and potential clinical intervention.
analysis.limitations: The paper is abstract‑only, provides no detailed methods or systematic data, and bases its therapeutic suggestion on limited case reports.
